title: Haze in Singapore: Air quality back in the unhealthy range - Yahoo News Singapore

 Laura Chia Updated Fri, 23 October 2026 at 11:11 pm UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Hazy conditions seen in Clementi at about 11.10am on Oct 24. SINGAPORE – The air quality across the island deteriorated overnight, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) recording unhealthy levels of air pollution early on Oct 24.
 At 7am, the PSI readings were 115 in the north and south regions, 117 in the east, 142 in the west and 133 in the central region.
 The PM2.5 readings – which are gauged hourly and reflect the current air quality – were also elevated across the country. At 7am, the PM2.5 readings were 79 in the north, 78 (south), 68 (east), 107 (west) and 94 (central).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, the air quality improved later in the day. At 5.30pm, only the PM2.5 in the west (97) was in the elevated band. The other regions were in the normal band – 55 or lower – with readings ranging from 33 to 53.
 PSI readings, though, remained in the unhealthy range across the island at 5.30pm, ranging from 108 to 151.
 There had been a brief respite from the haze early on Oct 23, when PSI readings were in the good to moderate range and PM2.5 levels were in the normal range.
 Singapore has been experiencing unhealthy air quality, denoted by 24-hour PSI readings above 101, since Oct 5.
 The 24-hour PSI, which is a rolling index of six key air pollutants, reflects air quality in Singapore over the past day.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When air quality breaches this threshold, people, especially the elderly, children and those with health issues, should start scaling down outdoor activities.
 Forecast for Oct 25
 In its daily advisory on the evening of Oct 24, the National Environment Agency (NEA) said moderate to unhealthy air quality is expected on Oct 25, with the PSI forecast to be in the range of 80 to 130.
 Smoke haze from Sumatra was seen drifting towards Singapore and was also observed over Kalimantan on Oct 24, NEA said.
 On Oct 25, winds are expected to blow from the south-west or west, which could limit transport of smoke haze to Singapore. Showers are expected over Singapore and the surrounding region which may help with the haze conditions, added NEA.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Winds are winds are expected to continue blowing from the south-west or west on Oct 26 and 27, and with showers expected over Singapore and the vicinity, the haze situation is "likely to improve", added the agency.
